title: Ahaziah Seeks Baal-zebub
image_prompt: After Ahab’s death, Moab rebels against Israel. Ahaziah falls through a lattice in his upper chamber at Samaria and is injured. He sends messengers to Ekron to inquire of Baal-zebub whether he will recover. Show attendants helping the king, a palace balcony, and messengers preparing for the road; no graphic injury.

title: Elijah Announces Ahaziah’s Death
image_prompt: Elijah intercepts the messengers and declares that Ahaziah will die because he sought an oracle from Baal-zebub instead of the God of Israel. Two captains and their companies approach Elijah on the hill and are consumed by fire from heaven; a third captain approaches humbly and is spared. Elijah delivers the word, and Ahaziah dies, succeeded by Jehoram. Show supernatural fire reverently and without graphic detail.

title: Elijah and Elisha Cross the Jordan
image_prompt: Elijah and Elisha travel from Gilgal to Bethel, Jericho, and the Jordan. At each stop Elijah tells Elisha to remain, but Elisha refuses to leave him. Groups of prophets watch from a distance. At the river, Elijah rolls up his mantle and strikes the water, which parts so the two cross on dry ground.

title: Elijah Is Taken Up
image_prompt: Elisha asks for a double portion of Elijah’s spirit. A chariot and horses of fire separate them, and Elijah is taken up by a whirlwind. Elisha cries out in grief, tears his clothes, and picks up Elijah’s fallen mantle. He strikes the Jordan with it and asks where the LORD God of Elijah is; the waters divide again. Depict the ascent as miraculous and reverent, not machinery.

title: Elisha Is Recognized and Heals Jericho’s Water
image_prompt: The sons of the prophets recognize that Elijah’s spirit rests on Elisha, though their search for Elijah’s body finds nothing. Elisha heals Jericho’s spring by casting salt from a new cruse into it. On the road to Bethel, youths mock him; he pronounces judgment in the LORD’s name and two bears emerge from the woods. Keep the bear incident non-graphic and unsensational.

title: The Kings Face a Water Crisis
image_prompt: Jehoram of Israel rules while still following Jeroboam’s sins. Moab rebels, so Jehoram enlists Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom. The allied armies travel through the wilderness for seven days and run short of water. Show the three kings at a dry ravine, exhausted soldiers and animals, and the urgent crisis.

title: Elisha Promises Water
image_prompt: Elisha rebukes Jehoram’s reliance on his parents’ prophets but agrees to inquire of the LORD for Jehoshaphat’s sake. A minstrel plays, and Elisha receives the LORD’s word: trenches must be dug. Though no wind or rain appears, the valley fills with water by morning. Show the musician, the trenches, and soldiers watching water arrive unexpectedly.

title: Moab Is Defeated and the Armies Withdraw
image_prompt: The Moabites see sunlight reflecting from the water and mistake it for blood, believing the allied kings have slaughtered one another. They advance to plunder but are repelled. The allies devastate Moab, but the Moabite king’s desperate sacrifice of his eldest son on the wall causes great indignation, and the armies withdraw. Depict this disturbing event with restraint and no graphic detail.

title: The Widow’s Oil Is Multiplied
image_prompt: A widow of the sons of the prophets says a creditor will take her two sons as servants. Elisha asks what she has; only a pot of oil remains. He tells her to borrow empty vessels, shut the door with her sons, and pour. The oil continues until every vessel is full; she sells it to pay the debt and live on the rest. Show a modest home filled with jars and the family’s astonishment.

title: The Shunammite’s Hospitality and Promise
image_prompt: A wealthy woman of Shunem regularly feeds Elisha and prepares a small upper room with a bed, table, stool, and lamp. Learning she has no son, Elisha promises she will embrace a child at the appointed season. Show the carefully furnished chamber, the woman’s hospitality, and her restrained disbelief as the promise is given.

title: The Child Dies and Gehazi Is Sent
image_prompt: The promised child grows, then becomes ill in the field and dies in his mother’s lap. She lays him on Elisha’s bed and hurries to Mount Carmel. Elisha sends Gehazi ahead with his staff, but it does not awaken the child. Keep the death non-graphic; focus on the mother’s grief, urgency, and determination.

title: Elisha Restores the Child
image_prompt: Elisha enters the room, shuts the door, and prays to the LORD. He stretches himself upon the child, who grows warm, sneezes seven times, and opens his eyes. Elisha calls the mother, who bows in gratitude and takes up her son. Show the intimate miracle quietly and reverently, without exaggerated effects.

title: Stew Is Purified and Bread Is Multiplied
image_prompt: During famine, Elisha tells the prophets to prepare stew. Wild gourds make it unsafe, but Elisha adds flour and it becomes harmless. Later a man brings twenty barley loaves and fresh grain; Elisha orders the food shared among a hundred men, and there is food left according to the LORD’s word. Show the community meal, cooking pots, loaves, and unexpected abundance.

title: Naaman Seeks Healing
image_prompt: Naaman, commander of Syria’s army, is a great man but has a serious skin disease. A captive Israelite girl tells Naaman’s wife that the prophet in Samaria could heal him. The Syrian king sends a letter and gifts to Israel’s king, who fears it is a pretext for war. Show Naaman’s attendants, the diplomatic letter, and Israel’s king tearing his robes in alarm.

title: Naaman Washes in the Jordan
image_prompt: Elisha tells Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan. Naaman arrives with horses and chariots but becomes angry when Elisha sends only a messenger, expecting a dramatic gesture. His servants reason with him, and he humbles himself to wash in the Jordan; his skin is restored. Show the river, attendants, and Naaman’s astonishment without clinical detail.

title: Naaman Confesses the LORD
image_prompt: Naaman returns to Elisha and declares there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. Elisha refuses his gifts. Naaman asks for earth to take home and for understanding about accompanying his king into the house of Rimmon; Elisha sends him away in peace. Show Naaman’s humility and the prophet’s refusal of payment.

title: Gehazi’s Greed Is Exposed
image_prompt: Gehazi secretly pursues Naaman, invents a story to obtain silver and clothing, then hides the goods. Elisha confronts him, revealing that he knows what happened. Gehazi leaves affected by Naaman’s disease. Portray the consequence soberly and respectfully, focusing on deceit, greed, and prophetic discernment rather than graphic symptoms.

title: The Borrowed Axe Head Floats
image_prompt: The sons of the prophets ask Elisha to help enlarge their meeting place near the Jordan. While cutting wood, a borrowed iron axe head falls into the water. Elisha throws a stick into the place, and the iron floats. Show the riverside worksite, the empty axe handle, the recovered tool, and the workers’ astonishment.

title: Elisha Reveals Syria’s Plans and Shows Mercy
image_prompt: The king of Syria repeatedly plans ambushes, but Elisha warns Israel’s king. Syrian forces surround Dothan; Elisha’s servant fears, so Elisha prays and the servant sees the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire. Elisha leads blinded Syrians to Samaria, where their sight returns. Israel’s king feeds them and sends them home rather than killing them. Render the heavenly host as a majestic vision and captives humanely.

title: Samaria Suffers a Terrible Siege
image_prompt: Ben-hadad besieges Samaria, causing severe famine. The king hears of desperate acts and tears his clothes, revealing sackcloth beneath. A woman appeals over a tragic dispute involving her child; keep the account non-graphic and focus on famine’s horror and the king’s anguish. The king blames Elisha and sends a messenger, while Elisha sits with the elders and anticipates the king’s arrival.

title: Elisha Predicts Abundance
image_prompt: At the height of Samaria’s famine, Elisha announces that by the next day food will be sold cheaply at the city gate. A royal officer doubts that the LORD could open windows in heaven to make it happen. Elisha says the officer will see it but not eat of it. Show the crowded gate, exhausted citizens, and the officer’s skeptical expression.

title: Four Lepers Discover the Empty Syrian Camp
image_prompt: Four men with a skin disease decide to surrender to the Syrian camp rather than starve. At dusk they find it abandoned: the LORD has caused the Syrians to hear the sound of a great army. The men eat, drink, and hide silver and clothing, then realize they should tell the city. Show empty tents, abandoned supplies, and the men wrestling with conscience.

title: Samaria Finds Food and the Officer Dies
image_prompt: The king cautiously sends scouts, who find evidence of the Syrians’ hurried flight. The people rush out and plunder the camp; food becomes available at the gate exactly as Elisha predicted. The skeptical officer is trampled at the gate and dies, fulfilling the prophecy. Depict the crowd without graphic injury and close on the contrast between fulfilled promise and unbelief.

title: The Shunammite Recovers Her Land
image_prompt: Elisha warns the Shunammite woman to leave the land during a seven-year famine. When she returns, she appeals to the king for her house and land. Gehazi is recounting Elisha’s miracles, including the restoration of her son, and the king orders her property and its produce restored. Show the woman before the king, her son nearby, and officials reviewing the land claim.

title: Hazael Becomes King of Syria
image_prompt: Elisha visits Damascus while Ben-hadad is ill. The king sends Hazael with a gift and asks whether he will recover. Elisha says the illness need not kill him but reveals that Hazael will become king and bring suffering to Israel; Elisha weeps. Hazael returns, kills Ben-hadad, and takes the throne. Keep the killing non-graphic and focus on the grim transition of power.

title: Jehoram Reigns in Judah
image_prompt: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat becomes king of Judah and follows the ways of Ahab’s house, partly because he married into that family. Edom revolts and establishes its own king, and Libnah also rebels. Show Judah’s court, southern borderlands slipping from control, and the strain on the kingdom.

title: Ahaziah Joins Joram in Battle
image_prompt: Ahaziah son of Jehoram becomes king of Judah and follows Ahab’s house. He joins Joram son of Ahab against Hazael of Syria at Ramoth-gilead. Joram is wounded and goes to Jezreel to recover, while Ahaziah visits him. Show the allied camp, the wounded king being carried toward Jezreel, and the political alliance.

title: Jehu Is Anointed King
image_prompt: Elisha sends a young prophet to Ramoth-gilead with oil and instructions to anoint Jehu privately. The prophet declares judgment on Ahab’s house and flees. Jehu’s fellow officers ask what happened; when he tells them, they spread garments on the steps, blow a trumpet, and proclaim him king. Show secrecy turning into a sudden public transfer of power.

title: Joram and Ahaziah Are Struck Down
image_prompt: Jehu drives furiously toward Jezreel. Joram of Israel and Ahaziah of Judah ride out to meet him; Joram asks whether there is peace. Jehu condemns Jezebel’s wickedness and shoots Joram with an arrow; Ahaziah flees but is pursued and mortally wounded. Keep violence non-graphic and emphasize the chariot encounter and collapse of Ahab’s dynasty.

title: Jezebel’s Death Fulfills the Prophecy
image_prompt: Jezebel adorns herself and looks from a window as Jehu enters Jezreel. At his command, servants throw her down; show the event from a respectful distance without graphic detail. Jehu orders burial, but only her skull, feet, and hands remain, fulfilling Elijah’s prophecy. Include the palace window, courtyard, and stunned attendants.

title: Ahab’s Descendants Are Judged
image_prompt: Jehu sends letters to Samaria’s rulers and guardians challenging them to defend Ahab’s sons. Frightened, they submit and carry out his order; the heads are brought to Jezreel in baskets. Depict the political terror and aftermath without graphic display: covered baskets, anxious officials, and Jehu addressing the people about the fulfillment of the LORD’s word.

title: Jehu Destroys the Remaining House of Ahab
image_prompt: On the road to Samaria, Jehu meets relatives of Ahaziah traveling to visit the royal family; they are captured and killed. Jehu continues to Samaria and removes those remaining of Ahab’s house. Show the mounted company on a dusty road and the collapse of the royal network, without graphic violence.

title: Jehu Destroys Baal’s Temple
image_prompt: Jehu announces a great sacrifice to Baal and gathers Baal’s worshippers in the temple. He ensures that no servant of the LORD is present, outfits worshippers in distinct garments, and stations guards at the doors. Once the ceremony begins, his men strike the worshippers and destroy the temple and sacred pillar, turning the site into a refuse place. Depict the purge without graphic detail.

title: Jehu’s Mixed Legacy
image_prompt: Jehu removes Baal worship but continues the golden-calf worship at Bethel and Dan. Hazael takes territory east of the Jordan. The LORD acknowledges Jehu’s judgment on Ahab’s house and promises four generations on Israel’s throne, yet Jehu does not walk fully in the law. Show the ruined Baal shrine beside a calf shrine still standing, and the aging king’s court.

title: Athaliah Seizes the Throne
image_prompt: After Ahaziah’s death, Athaliah attempts to destroy the royal heirs. Jehosheba hides the infant Joash and his nurse in a bedchamber, then conceals him in the house of the LORD for six years. Show a tense palace corridor, the nurse protecting the child, and the sanctuary’s shadowed rooms as refuge.

title: Joash Is Revealed and Crowned
image_prompt: In the seventh year, Jehoiada gathers captains, guards, and Levites and positions them around the temple. He brings out the king’s son; Joash receives the crown and testimony, is anointed, and the people clap and shout, “God save the king.” Show the temple court crowded with guards and worshippers, with the young king protected at the center.

title: Athaliah Falls and the Covenant Is Renewed
image_prompt: Athaliah hears the people and enters the temple crying treason. Jehoiada orders her removed from the sacred precinct and she is put to death outside it. The priest makes a covenant among the LORD, king, and people; Baal’s temple is destroyed, and Joash is taken to the palace throne. Keep the execution non-graphic and emphasize renewed worship and public order.

title: Joash Orders Temple Repairs
image_prompt: Joash reigns in Judah and does right while Jehoiada instructs him. He orders priests to use collected sacred offerings to repair the temple, but the work is delayed. Show weathered stonework, damaged timber, worn doors, and priests discussing a dependable repair fund.

title: The Temple Repair Chest
image_prompt: Jehoiada places a chest with a hole in its lid beside the altar, and priests deposit money brought to the LORD’s house. The king’s secretary and high priest weigh and distribute funds to carpenters, builders, masons, and stonecutters. Show honest craftsmen restoring the sanctuary with tools, stone blocks, timber, and accounting scales.

title: Joash Pays Tribute and Is Killed
image_prompt: Hazael of Syria threatens Jerusalem after taking Gath. Joash sends sacred and royal treasures to Hazael, who withdraws. Joash’s servants conspire against him and kill him at the house of Millo; Amaziah succeeds him. Depict the political crisis and death without graphic detail, closing on the succession.

title: Jehoahaz and Israel’s Oppression
image_prompt: Jehoahaz son of Jehu reigns in Israel and follows Jeroboam’s sins. Syria oppresses Israel and reduces its military strength; Jehoahaz seeks the LORD, and a deliverer is provided, though the people do not abandon their sins. Show a diminished Israelite force, Syrian pressure at the frontier, and the king praying in a modest chamber.

title: Jehoash Succeeds Jehoahaz
image_prompt: Jehoash son of Jehoahaz reigns in Samaria and continues the sins of Jeroboam. The account notes his wars with Amaziah of Judah and his death, with Jeroboam II succeeding him. Show the royal court and military advisers, conveying a kingdom caught in recurring conflict and idolatrous practice.

title: Elisha’s Final Prophecy
image_prompt: Elisha is ill with the illness from which he will die. Jehoash visits and weeps, calling him the chariot of Israel and its horsemen. Elisha tells him to shoot an arrow eastward, symbolizing victory over Syria, then to strike the ground with arrows. Jehoash strikes three times and stops; Elisha is displeased because he will win only three victories. Show the prophet on his bed, the king at the window, and the bow and arrows.

title: A Dead Man Revives and Cities Are Recovered
image_prompt: After Elisha’s death, a burial party hurriedly places a man in Elisha’s tomb when Moabite raiders appear. When the dead man touches Elisha’s bones, he revives and stands. Later Jehoash recovers cities from Ben-hadad son of Hazael, fulfilling the LORD’s word. Keep the resurrection reverent and non-graphic; show the tomb, startled mourners, and later restored towns.

title: Amaziah Reigns and Defeats Edom
image_prompt: Amaziah of Judah does right, though not like David. He executes his father’s killers but spares their children according to the law. He defeats Edom in the Valley of Salt and captures Sela, renaming it Joktheel. Show judicial restraint, an arid southern campaign, and soldiers returning from victory.

title: Amaziah Challenges Jehoash
image_prompt: Amaziah challenges Jehoash of Israel. Jehoash answers with a parable of a thistle and a cedar, warning against pride. They meet at Beth-shemesh; Judah is defeated, Amaziah captured, Jerusalem’s wall breached, and treasures taken from temple and palace. Depict defeat and damage without graphic combat.

title: Kings Die and Jeroboam II Expands Israel
image_prompt: Jehoash of Israel dies and Jeroboam II succeeds him. Amaziah later dies in a conspiracy at Lachish; Azariah (Uzziah) becomes king and rebuilds Elath. Show the political transitions through royal gates, messengers, and the southern port being rebuilt.

title: Jeroboam II’s Long Reign
image_prompt: Jeroboam II restores territory from the entrance of Hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the LORD’s word through Jonah son of Amittai. The text notes Israel’s affliction and the LORD’s compassion despite its sins. Show restored border towns and a prophet surveying the land, while retaining signs of spiritual decline.

title: Azariah Reigns in Judah
image_prompt: Azariah son of Amaziah does right, though high places remain. The LORD afflicts him with a skin disease, and he lives separately while Jotham governs the palace and judges the people. Show Azariah apart from the court and Jotham carrying out administrative duties; portray illness respectfully without graphic detail.

title: Zechariah’s Brief Reign
image_prompt: Zechariah son of Jeroboam reigns in Israel for six months and continues Jeroboam’s sins. Shallum conspires against him and kills him publicly, ending Jehu’s dynasty after four generations as the LORD had promised. Show the unstable northern court and abrupt transfer of power without graphic violence.

title: Shallum and Menahem
image_prompt: Shallum reigns only one month before Menahem attacks Samaria from Tirzah, kills Shallum, and seizes the throne. Menahem’s campaign against Tiphsah is harsh; convey the brutality through damaged gates, frightened residents, and smoke rather than explicit injuries.

title: Menahem Pays Assyria
image_prompt: Menahem reigns ten years and does evil. Pul, king of Assyria, invades; Menahem pays him a large sum of silver, levied from wealthy men, to secure support. Show Assyrian envoys, tribute weighed on scales, and the kingdom’s growing dependence on a foreign empire.

title: Pekahiah Is Killed
image_prompt: Pekahiah son of Menahem continues Israel’s sins. Pekah, one of his captains, conspires with fifty men from Gilead and kills him in the palace citadel at Samaria, then takes the throne. Depict the coup through shadowed corridors and shocked guards, without graphic detail.

title: Pekah and the Assyrian Invasion
image_prompt: Pekah reigns and continues Jeroboam’s sins. Tiglath-pileser of Assyria captures towns and carries inhabitants into exile; Hoshea conspires against Pekah and kills him, succeeding him as king. Show Assyrian troops, deportation lines treated with dignity, and Israel’s weakening borders.

title: Jotham Reigns in Judah
image_prompt: Jotham does right, though high places remain. He builds the upper gate of the house of the LORD and strengthens parts of Jerusalem, while Syria and Israel begin pressuring Judah. Show construction work, the king’s court, and looming regional threats.

title: Ahaz Turns to Assyria
image_prompt: Ahaz of Judah follows the ways of Israel’s kings and even makes his son pass through fire. Rezin of Syria and Pekah of Israel attack Jerusalem but cannot take it. Ahaz sends silver and gold from the temple and palace to Tiglath-pileser of Assyria, asking for rescue. Show a frightened king, besieged walls, and tribute leaving Jerusalem.

title: Ahaz Copies the Altar of Damascus
image_prompt: Ahaz visits Damascus, sees an altar, and sends its design to Uriah the priest. The priest builds a matching altar, and Ahaz orders sacrifices on it, moving the bronze altar aside. Show the new altar being constructed in the temple court, with priests and craftsmen, emphasizing unauthorized changes to sacred worship.

title: Temple Furnishings Are Altered
image_prompt: Ahaz removes or modifies temple fixtures and changes arrangements to please the king of Assyria. The account records his death and Hezekiah’s accession. Show sacred furnishings being repositioned, the temple court diminished in splendor, and the transition to a new reign.

title: Samaria Falls to Assyria
image_prompt: Hoshea becomes king of Israel, later seeks Egypt’s help and withholds tribute from Assyria. Shalmaneser arrests him and besieges Samaria for three years, eventually taking the city and deporting Israelites to distant regions. Show siege ramps, Assyrian troops, exhausted defenders, and deportees leaving in a solemn procession.

title: Why Israel Went into Exile
image_prompt: The narrator explains that Israel was exiled for sinning against the LORD, adopting surrounding nations’ practices, building high places, worshipping idols, and rejecting prophetic warnings. Use a sequence-like composition of unauthorized shrines, carved images, neglected covenant worship, and prophets calling people back. Make clear this is a theological summary, not a single simultaneous event.

title: Foreign Peoples Settle Samaria
image_prompt: Assyria resettles people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim in Samaria. Lions attack some settlers, who interpret this as a sign that they do not know the god of the land. An Israelite priest is sent to teach them, but they retain a mixed pattern of worship. Show diverse families settling among the hills and a priest teaching at a local shrine.

title: Mixed Worship in Samaria
image_prompt: The chapter recalls covenant commands Israel had broken and describes settlers who fear the LORD while continuing to serve their own images. Show the tension between public reverence and household idols, with Samaria’s hills in the background and no suggestion that the mixed worship is approved.

title: Hezekiah Reforms Judah
image_prompt: Hezekiah trusts the LORD, removes high places, breaks sacred pillars, cuts down the Asherah, and destroys the bronze serpent because people have burned incense to it. Show workers removing unauthorized worship objects and the bronze serpent being taken from its pedestal, with Hezekiah directing reform reverently.

title: Assyria Advances and Hezekiah Pays Tribute
image_prompt: The account recalls Samaria’s fall and then describes Sennacherib’s invasion of Judah. Hezekiah submits and pays tribute, stripping silver from the temple and gold from its doors. Show Assyrian forces advancing through fortified towns and temple treasure carefully removed under pressure of war.

title: The Rabshakeh Challenges Jerusalem
image_prompt: Sennacherib sends a great army to Jerusalem with the Rabshakeh, who speaks loudly in Hebrew to the people on the wall. He mocks Hezekiah’s trust in Egypt and the LORD, claiming Assyria is unstoppable. Show the envoy before the city wall, officials Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah listening in distress, and people watching from above.

title: The People Hear the Threat
image_prompt: Officials ask the Rabshakeh to speak in Aramaic, but he continues in Hebrew so the people will hear. He offers food and safety if they surrender and claims the LORD cannot deliver them. The people remain silent by the king’s command; the officials return to Hezekiah with torn garments. Show the siege line and the grave report at the palace.

title: Hezekiah Seeks Isaiah’s Counsel
image_prompt: Hezekiah tears his clothes, wears sackcloth, and sends officials to Isaiah asking him to pray for the remnant. Isaiah replies that the LORD will cause the Assyrian king to hear a report and return home, where he will fall by the sword. Show the king in mourning, messengers moving urgently through Jerusalem, and Isaiah speaking with assurance.

title: Hezekiah Spreads the Letter Before the LORD
image_prompt: Sennacherib sends another threatening message, claiming no god has delivered nations from Assyria. Hezekiah takes the letter to the house of the LORD and spreads it before God, praying for deliverance so all kingdoms may know the LORD alone is God. Show the letter open on the temple floor and the king kneeling earnestly.

title: Isaiah Announces Jerusalem Will Stand
image_prompt: Isaiah declares that Assyria has mocked the Holy One of Israel, but its pride will be judged. The LORD promises Sennacherib will not enter Jerusalem or shoot an arrow there; the city will be defended for the LORD’s sake and David’s. Show Isaiah delivering the oracle, Jerusalem’s walls standing firm, and the Assyrian camp beyond the city.

title: The Assyrian Camp Is Struck
image_prompt: That night the angel of the LORD strikes the Assyrian camp; show abandoned tents and stillness at dawn without graphic casualties. Sennacherib withdraws to Nineveh and is later killed by his sons while worshipping in the house of Nisroch. Depict the retreat and the distant temple interior without graphic violence.

title: Hezekiah Is Healed
image_prompt: Hezekiah becomes gravely ill, and Isaiah tells him to set his house in order. The king turns to the wall and prays with tears; the LORD sends Isaiah back with a promise of fifteen more years and deliverance for Jerusalem. A cake of figs is placed on the boil, and Hezekiah asks for a sign. Show the bedside, Isaiah’s return, and the quiet atmosphere of prayer.

title: Babylonian Envoys and Isaiah’s Warning
image_prompt: The king of Babylon sends envoys and a gift after hearing of Hezekiah’s illness. Hezekiah shows them treasures, armory, and storehouses. Isaiah warns that these things will one day be carried to Babylon and some descendants will be taken into service. Hezekiah accepts the word, noting there will be peace in his days; close with his death and Manasseh’s succession.

title: Manasseh Fills Jerusalem with Idolatry
image_prompt: Manasseh reigns for fifty-five years, rebuilds high places, raises altars to Baal, makes an Asherah, worships the host of heaven, and places idolatrous objects in the temple. Show the sanctuary precinct corrupted by foreign cult symbols and royal patronage while faithful worshippers look on in distress. Keep focus on religious violation rather than sensational imagery.

title: Judgment Is Pronounced on Judah
image_prompt: Prophets announce disaster because of Manasseh’s abominations and bloodshed; Jerusalem will be measured with the line of Samaria and the plummet of Ahab’s house. Manasseh dies and is buried in the garden of his house; Amon succeeds him. Show a prophetic warning before the city and a quiet royal burial.

title: Amon’s Short Reign and Conspiracy
image_prompt: Amon follows his father’s evil practices and serves idols. His servants conspire and kill him in his house, but the people execute the conspirators and make Josiah king. Show the palace coup in shadow and the public affirmation of young Josiah, emphasizing instability and succession without graphic detail.

title: Josiah Orders Temple Repairs
image_prompt: Josiah becomes king at eight years old and does right in the LORD’s sight. In his eighteenth year he sends Shaphan to Hilkiah with collected money for temple repairs, instructing that workers be paid honestly. Show the young king with advisers, temple officials counting contributions, and craftsmen repairing old stonework and timber.

title: The Book of the Law Is Found
image_prompt: Hilkiah reports that he has found the book of the law in the house of the LORD. Shaphan reads it before Josiah, who tears his clothes and recognizes that the nation has not obeyed. Show the scroll open in a quiet chamber, the king listening with mounting distress, and officials gathered around.

title: Huldah Confirms Judgment
image_prompt: Josiah sends officials to inquire of the LORD through Huldah the prophetess. She declares that disaster will come because of Judah’s idolatry, but because Josiah humbled himself and wept, he will not see the calamity in his lifetime. Show Huldah speaking with authority to the royal delegation and the king awaiting the answer.

title: Josiah Renews the Covenant
image_prompt: Josiah gathers elders, priests, prophets, and the people at the temple and reads the covenant book aloud. He stands by a pillar and pledges to follow the LORD with all his heart and soul; the people join him. Show the crowded temple court, scroll held open, and solemn public commitment.

title: Josiah Removes Idolatry
image_prompt: Josiah orders removal of vessels made for Baal, Asherah, and the host of heaven, removes idolatrous priests, tears down cult rooms, and defiles high places. He destroys altars built by earlier kings. Depict reformers carrying objects from the temple and dismantling shrines without glorifying destruction.

title: Bethel’s Altar and the Prophecy Fulfilled
image_prompt: Josiah destroys Jeroboam’s altar at Bethel and burns the high place. He notices a tomb and orders the bones left undisturbed because a man of God foretold the act. The text also recounts action against high-place priests; show the solemn fulfillment of prophecy without graphic detail.

title: Passover Is Kept
image_prompt: Josiah commands the people to keep Passover according to the covenant book, and a great Passover is held. Yet the LORD’s anger against Judah’s accumulated sins is not turned away because of Manasseh’s deeds. Show families, priests, and Levites in a reverent Passover gathering, with the shadow of judgment still present.

title: Josiah Dies at Megiddo
image_prompt: Pharaoh Necho travels north, and Josiah goes out to meet him at Megiddo. Josiah is wounded by archers and dies; his servants carry him in a chariot to Jerusalem, where he is buried. The people make Jehoahaz king. Keep the wound non-graphic and show the mourning procession.

title: Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim
image_prompt: Jehoahaz reigns three months before Pharaoh Necho imprisons him and imposes tribute. Necho makes Eliakim king and changes his name to Jehoiakim; Jehoiakim taxes the land to pay the tribute and does evil. Show Egyptian authority at court, the renaming ceremony, and burdensome tribute collection.

title: Babylon Rises Against Judah
image_prompt: During Jehoiakim’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar invades Judah, and bands of Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites raid the land. These events fulfill the LORD’s word; Egypt no longer ventures out as Babylon becomes dominant. Show raiding forces across the countryside, pressured villages, and Babylon’s growing imperial reach.

title: Jehoiachin and Jerusalem Are Taken
image_prompt: Jehoiachin reigns three months before Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem. The king, his mother, servants, officials, and leading people surrender and are taken captive. Babylon carries away temple and palace treasures and takes skilled workers and soldiers into exile; Zedekiah is made king. Show a sorrowful deportation procession, catalogued treasures, and the city under foreign control.

title: Zedekiah Rebels
image_prompt: Zedekiah reigns in Jerusalem and does evil, as Jehoiakim had done. He rebels against Babylon, setting the stage for the final siege. Show Zedekiah in a tense council chamber, messengers and military plans on a table, and Jerusalem’s threatened walls in the distance.

title: Jerusalem Is Besieged and Zedekiah Captured
image_prompt: Nebuchadnezzar’s army surrounds Jerusalem in Zedekiah’s ninth year. The siege continues until famine is severe and a breach is made in the wall. Zedekiah and his soldiers flee by night but are overtaken near Jericho. He is brought before the Babylonian king; his sons are killed before him, he is blinded, and he is taken to Babylon. Keep violence non-graphic and emphasize the city’s collapse.

title: The Temple and City Are Burned
image_prompt: Nebuzaradan enters Jerusalem and burns the house of the LORD, the royal palace, and important buildings. Babylonian troops break down the city walls and deport many people, leaving only some of the poorest to tend vineyards and fields. Show smoke over Jerusalem, the ruined temple complex, broken walls, and a small remnant left behind.

title: The Temple Vessels Are Carried Away
image_prompt: Babylonian soldiers break the bronze pillars, bronze sea, and movable stands, carrying the metal to Babylon. They take pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and other vessels, including bronze and gold objects from the temple. Show craftsmen dismantling the great bronze furnishings and officials cataloguing sacred objects; do not confuse these furnishings with the Ark, which is not mentioned here.

title: Judah’s Leaders Are Executed and Exiled
image_prompt: Nebuzaradan captures the chief priest, second priest, temple doorkeepers, military officials, and other leading men. They are taken to the king of Babylon at Riblah and executed; the remaining people are carried away from Judah. Depict the loss of leadership through a solemn line of captives and an emptied Jerusalem, without graphic execution detail.

title: Gedaliah Is Appointed and Assassinated
image_prompt: Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah over the people left in Judah. Gedaliah urges the people and captains to serve Babylon and live peacefully, but Ishmael son of Nethaniah assassinates him and those with him at Mizpah. Survivors flee to Egypt in fear of the Chaldeans. Show Gedaliah’s modest gathering, the assassination only implied, and frightened survivors preparing to leave.

title: Jehoiachin Is Released in Babylon
image_prompt: In the thirty-seventh year of Jehoiachin’s exile, Evil-merodach king of Babylon releases him from prison and treats him kindly. Jehoiachin receives honor above other captive kings, changes his prison garments, eats regularly at the king’s table, and receives a daily allowance for life. End with a quiet scene of the aged king at a royal table in Babylon, a note of mercy amid exile.
